definitions.explanation: A shallow box or pit filled with sand where children can play, typically found in playgrounds and parks.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}たちが{砂場|すなば}で{遊|あそ}んでいる。
examples.english: The children are playing in the sandbox.

examples.japanese: {砂場|すなば}で{砂|すな}のお{城|しろ}を{作|つく}った。
examples.english: I made a sand castle in the sandbox.

examples.japanese: {砂場|すなば}で{遊|あそ}んだ{後|あと}は{手|て}を{洗|あら}いなさい。
examples.english: Wash your hands after playing in the sandbox.

notes:
{砂場|すなば} is a sandbox or sandpit for children's play.

COMMON ACTIVITIES:
- {砂|すな}のお{城|しろ}を{作|つく}る (make a sand castle)
- {砂|すな}を{掘|ほ}る (dig in the sand)
- {砂|すな}{遊|あそ}び (sand play)
- {泥団子|どろだんご}を{作|つく}る (make mud balls)

COMMON TOOLS:
- バケツ (bucket)
- スコップ (small shovel)
- {砂型|すながた} (sand mold)
- {熊手|くまで} (rake)

HYGIENE NOTE:
Many Japanese parks cover sandboxes at night to prevent contamination from stray cats. Signs often remind children to wash their hands after playing.

RELATED PLAYGROUND EQUIPMENT:
- ぶらんこ (swing)
- {滑|すべ}り{台|だい} (slide)
- シーソー (seesaw)
